title: Looking for a Bride

full_text:
A prosperous young shepherd wished to marry, but could not choose between three sisters who were equally beautiful, polite, and well-favored. Unable to make up his mind, he sought counsel from his mother, an experienced and prudent woman.

"Invite all three sisters to our house for supper," advised the mother. "Set before them a large wheel of rich Swiss cheese, and watch carefully how they cut it."

The shepherd followed her counsel. The eldest sister took the cheese and greedily cut off a thick piece, eating the dirty rind and all in her haste. "She is too careless and untidy," observed the shepherd.

The second sister cut off the rind, but in her anxiety she cut so thick that half the good cheese was wasted and thrown onto the plate. "She is too wasteful and extravagant," thought the youth.

The third sister carefully trimmed only the thinnest layer of rind from the cheese, wasting not a crumb of the good curd while ensuring the cheese was cleanly prepared.

"She is both thrifty and neat," declared the young shepherd. He asked for the hand of the third sister, and they celebrated a wedding of great happiness, living in prosperous harmony and managing their household with practical wisdom.
moral: True character and domestic wisdom are revealed in how one handles the smallest things.

quiz.question: What is the central moral lesson taught in "Looking for a Bride"?
options: Presence of mind and quiet wisdom triumph over brute strength.
Acting in haste and anger without thinking
Believing rumors and flattery without proof
quiz.hint: Remember the moral lesson of this traditional story.

quiz.question: How do the characters overcome their challenge?
options: Through patience, calm reflection, and wisdom
By shouting loudly and blaming others
By running away from every problem
quiz.hint: Consider the virtues praised in world folklore.

quiz.question: What memorable conclusion does this story teach young readers?
options: Honesty, kindness, and clear thinking lead to peace
quiz.hint: Reflect upon the resolution of the story.
